## Nosana vLLM Inference — Battle-Tested Deployment Knowledge

Qwen3.5-27B-AWQ-4bit on Nosana DePIN has specific quirks that differ from standard OpenAI API:

1. THINKING MODE: Qwen3.5 enables thinking by default, returning empty content field with reasoning in a separate field. Fix: add enable_thinking=false to every request body.
2. DEVELOPER ROLE: Vercel AI SDK v5 sends 'developer' role messages. vLLM rejects this — only system/user/assistant allowed. Fix: map developer->system in proxy.
3. MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS: Vercel AI SDK sends max_completion_tokens but vLLM expects max_tokens. Fix: rename field and enforce minimum 4096 to prevent truncated responses.
4. EMBEDDINGS: vLLM inference endpoint doesn't serve embedding models. Fix: mock 1536-dimension zero vectors for embedding requests — ElizaOS needs embeddings for memory but they're not critical for security analysis.

## Nosana DePIN Security Architecture

Nosana decentralized GPU network provides unique security properties for code analysis:

1. PRIVACY: Code analyzed on Nosana never leaves the compute node — no data sent to centralized cloud providers (AWS/GCP/Azure). This solves the #1 objection enterprises have against AI security tools.
2. COST: RTX 3090 nodes cost $0.20-0.40/hour vs $1.00+/hour on hyperscalers. 80%+ cost reduction for continuous security scanning.
3. PERMISSIONLESS: No vendor lock-in, no enterprise sales call. Deploy with Builder Credits instantly.
4. CENSORSHIP-RESISTANT: Unlike cloud providers that may restrict security testing tools, Nosana nodes run any container without content restrictions.

## ElizaOS v2 + vLLM Compatibility — @ai-sdk/openai v2.x Breaking Change

CRITICAL: @ai-sdk/openai v2.x changed default API from Chat Completions (/v1/chat/completions) to Responses API (/v1/responses). The 'compatibility: compatible' option from v1.x was REMOVED.

Impact: ElizaOS plugin-openai calls provider.languageModel() which now hits /v1/responses — vLLM doesn't support this endpoint, returning 404.

Fix: Postinstall script patches node_modules to use provider.chat() instead of provider.languageModel(). This forces Chat Completions API which vLLM fully supports.

Lesson: When integrating open-source LLM backends with frameworks designed for OpenAI, always verify which API variant the SDK uses. The Responses API is OpenAI-proprietary.

## GitHub API Rate Limiting for Repository Scanning

Unauthenticated GitHub API requests are limited to 60/hour. Each SCAN_REPO action uses 2 API calls (repo info + tree). File contents are fetched via raw.githubusercontent.com which has NO rate limit.

Architecture: API calls only for metadata/tree discovery, raw.githubusercontent.com for all file content. This allows ~30 scans/hour without any token. With GITHUB_TOKEN (free, read-only): 5000 API calls/hour = unlimited scanning.

Security note: GITHUB_TOKEN should be fine-grained with Public Repositories (read-only) scope only. Never request write permissions for a scanning tool.

## CI/CD Security Patterns Found in Real Repository Scans

Tested against juice-shop, expressjs, and fastapi — findings calibrate with actual risk level:

1. pull_request_target workflow (HIGH): Runs PR code with repo write permissions and secrets access. Attacker can modify workflow via PR to exfiltrate secrets.
2. Dependabot ignoring major versions (MEDIUM): Creates false sense of security — major version bumps often contain security fixes.
3. npm install without --ignore-scripts (LOW): Postinstall scripts can execute arbitrary code during dependency installation.
4. Well-maintained repos (fastapi) correctly receive fewer findings — demonstrates calibrated analysis, not alert fatigue.

## Bun.serve() Production Constraints

Bun HTTP server has a hard limit: idleTimeout maximum is 255 seconds (not arbitrary). Setting higher values throws TypeError. For LLM inference proxies that need long timeouts (300s+ for complex analysis), use AbortController with custom timeout alongside the max idleTimeout=255.

Pattern: AbortController for request-level timeout (300s), idleTimeout for connection-level keepalive (255s max). These are complementary, not alternatives.
